summary: Frontend-only verification of the liabilities Excel export fix in SurplusSection.jsx. Since the preview DB does not have Deepak Mishra's family data, testing was performed by extracting the exact transformation logic (SECTION 4 LIABILITIES, SECTION 8 SUMMARY totalAnnualEMI, Financial Plan loan EMI split by type, and Cash Outflow loan EMI tenure gating) and executing it in the live browser context with production-mimic liability records: [{category:'home_loan', monthly_emi:24000, num_installments:240}, {category:'home_loan', monthly_emi:37000, num_installments:168}]. All expected outputs matched.
critical_code_review_comments: SurplusSection.jsx is 3980 lines — well above the 700-line guideline. Consider extracting the Excel export logic (Data Sheet + Cash Flow + Portfolio sheets) into a dedicated module (e.g. utils/exportSurplusExcel.js) with a small helper to normalize liability fields (getLoanEmi, getLoanTenure, getLoanCategory) so future field-name drift is centralized in one place.

The same field-priority expression `parseFloat(l.monthly_emi) || parseFloat(l.emi_amount)` is duplicated in 4 places (lines 2933, 3010, 3121, 3337). Same for num_installments/remaining_tenure and category/loan_type. Extract as `normalizeLiability(l)` helper to avoid future divergence bugs like the one just fixed.

In the loan-type classifier (line 3120), only 'home', 'vehicle'/'car' branches exist — everything else (including business_loan, education_loan, gold_loan) is bucketed as personalLoan. Consider explicit mapping to avoid mislabeling in reports.

seed_data_creation: None. Used in-memory production-mimic liability data injected via page.evaluate.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The fix in SurplusSection.jsx lines 2933-2938, 3010, 3120-3122, and 3336-3338 correctly prioritizes 'l.category' → 'l.loan_type', 'l.monthly_emi' → 'l.emi_amount', 'l.num_installments' → 'l.remaining_tenure'. Verified with Deepak Mishra's exact production data structure: 2 home loans (24k/240mo, 37k/168mo) produce correct LIABILITIES rows (both 'Home Loan'), Total Annual EMI = 7,32,000 in FINANCIAL SUMMARY, home-loan bucket in Financial Plan = 7,32,000 (nothing miscategorized as vehicle/personal), and cash-outflow correctly ends the 37k EMI at year 14 and 24k EMI at year 20. Backward compatibility with legacy field names (loan_type/emi_amount/remaining_tenure) also verified.
rca of the issue: Root cause: schema drift between DataGathering 'liabilities' collection (writes category / monthly_emi / num_installments) and legacy Excel export code (was reading loan_type / emi_amount / remaining_tenure). Because JS `undefined || undefined` short-circuits to 0/empty, existing liabilities were silently omitted from the Excel data sheet AND from the Financial Plan cash-outflows AND from the totalAnnualEMI summary. Fix: OR-chain now reads new fields first, old fields as fallback, giving both correctness on new data and backward compatibility. Verified end-to-end via in-browser evaluation of the exact export logic with production data.
